# Week 4 — SOC Dashboard Guide

**File:** `Week-4/Dashboard/index.html`. Double-click to open it; it works offline, with no
server and no internet.
**Data:** `Week-4/Dashboard/dashboard_data.js`, regenerated by `python -B Week-4/IR/ir_cli.py build`.
Never edit it by hand: change the data or the decisions, then rebuild.

## What the dashboard is for

The dashboard is the one-screen view of the whole capstone. It shows:
- what was detected (Week 2);
- what the SOAR layer did (Week 3);
- how the incident was handled (Week 4);
- how much the local AI can be trusted (Weeks 1, 2 and 4).

Everything on it is read from repository files. Hovering a number shows the file it came from,
and every view keeps the simulation boundary visible:
*Tabletop - historical lab data · Nothing auto-executed · Local AI only.*

## Views (left menu)

| View | What it shows | Where the data comes from |
|---|---|---|
| **Overview** | 8 KPI tiles (attack stages, evidence-backed cases, timeline events, indicators, SOAR tickets, proposals pending, local-AI analyses, trigger-to-AI-triage time); the 9-stage attack chain; the NIST lifecycle with progress bars; human-review status of all 19 cases; AI severity of the SIEM alerts; the simulation boundary | `Output/incident.json`, `Output/ir_lifecycle.json`, Week-2 evidence, Week-3 tickets |
| **Attack chain** | Swimlanes (rows = network / web / auth / endpoint / email, columns = stages S1–S9); cross-dataset overlaps (the same IP in two datasets); MITRE ATT&CK matrix coloured by confidence (observed pattern / candidate / hypothesis) | `Config/scenario.json`, `Config/attack_mapping.json`, `Output/observables.csv` |
| **Alerts & cases** | All 19 cases, filterable by domain, stage and kind (SIEM alert, dataset case, benign control). Clicking a row opens the case with facts, AI triage, human review, ATT&CK, source events, limitations, Week-3 tickets, response items and evidence files with SHA-256 | `Output/incident.json` |
| **Timeline** | Events in scenario order, grouped by stage, with the **original** dataset timestamp and its quality label (e.g. `no_year_no_timezone`); first 3 + last 3 events per case | `Output/incident_timeline.csv` (full list) |
| **Response (NIST)** | The 7 lifecycle phases and their computed status; every containment / eradication / recovery item with tier, read-only check result (T0), suggested decision, recorded decision and analyst; prohibited Tier-2 actions. **Copy** gives the exact `ir_cli.py decide` command for an item | `Output/ir_lifecycle.json`, `Output/t0_checks.json`, `Simulation/analyst_decisions.jsonl` |
| **SOAR (Week 3)** | The 4 playbooks (Tier 0 automatic steps, Tier 1 proposals, Tier 2 prohibited actions), the 7 tickets with their audit-log line counts, and the 18-row automation decision matrix | `Week-3/SOAR/playbooks/`, `Week-3/SOAR/tickets/`, `Week-3/SOAR/decision-matrix.md` |
| **AI quality (W1–W4)** | Week 1: manual quality and unsupported-fact severity per model. Week 2: validator flags by check and severity, human-review results, trigger-to-triage latency. Week 4: the 12 local-AI drafts with model, time, validator flags and review status; **View** opens the text (the corrected version when the analyst corrected it) | Week-1 benchmark CSVs, `Week-2/Results/AN-*/analysis.json`, `Output/ai_drafts/`, `Simulation/ai_draft_reviews.jsonl` |
| **Evidence & IOCs** | Observables split into *indicators* (IPs, domains, hashes, payload files) and *context* (lab hostnames, OS binaries, benign-control values), with scope (public / private / reserved) and reputation (always "not checked"); the evidence inventory with SHA-256 | `Output/observables.csv`, case evidence files |
| **Reports & run** | Links to the 7 reports, the open Week-2/Week-3 gates, and the commands to rebuild | `Reports/`, final reports of Weeks 2–3 |

## How to read the colours

- **Domain colours** (blue network, orange web, green auth, yellow endpoint, pink email) show
  identity only, and each one always carries its label.
- **Status dots:** green = complete / approved / done, amber = corrected / partial,
  orange = pending, red = rejected. Every dot has a text label.
- **Severity badges** (High / Medium) are the **AI's** rating from Week 2, not an analyst
  sign-off.
- **ATT&CK cells:** lighter blue = more certain (observed pattern), darker = less certain
  (hypothesis).

## Updating the dashboard

```cmd
python -B Week-4/IR/ir_cli.py build
```
Any decision (`decide`, `accept-suggestions`, `import-decisions`) or review (`review`) rebuilds
the dashboard automatically. Refresh the browser tab afterwards.

## Safety notes

- The evidence contains real XSS payloads. The page escapes every value before display, and a
  test checks for the escaping function.
- The page loads nothing from the internet; a test checks that it contains no external URLs.
- The **Copy** button only copies a command. The analyst still runs it and enters a name.
